steps.title: Every city has its icons
steps.body: Each of the 32 teams has its ==franchise legends== and today's stars. Fans pick a team and inherit its history, ==heroes and grudges== included.
steps.note: Every team's icons are in the Rulebook under Teams.

steps.title: Six rings each
steps.body: Pittsburgh and New England have the ==most titles: 6 each==. Pittsburgh's "Steel Curtain" won four in the '70s. New England's six all came with ==Tom Brady and coach Bill Belichick==.

steps.title: San Francisco
steps.body: Joe Montana, Jerry Rice and Steve Young won ==five titles in 14 seasons== with short, quick passes. Today's QB Brock Purdy was the ==very last pick== of his draft.
steps.note: The last pick each year is nicknamed Mr. Irrelevant.

steps.title: Green Bay
steps.body: The smallest city in the league, and the only team ==owned by its fans==. Players celebrate touchdowns by ==leaping into the stands==, and the championship trophy is named for its old coach, Vince Lombardi.

steps.title: Kansas City
steps.body: QB Patrick Mahomes and tight end Travis Kelce won ==3 titles in 5 seasons==. Kelce's relationship with ==Taylor Swift== brought a wave of new fans to the sport in 2023.

steps.title: The big game
steps.body: The championship game is usually the most-watched broadcast in the US each year. Plenty of viewers tune in for the ==halftime show== and the ==commercials== as much as the football.

steps.prompt: This touchdown celebration started with which team?
steps.explain: It's the Lambeau Leap, named for Green Bay's stadium. Players jump into the front row and fans grab them.

steps.prompt: Which two teams have won the most championships?
steps.explain: Pittsburgh and New England have six each. San Francisco and Dallas are next with five.
